researchCards.question: What does a record describe: a topic, a resource, or how to find one?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Compare invented descriptions of a general web archive, a topic-specific archive, and a book about building a search engine. Identify which scope note makes each case different.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Use the inspected scope directions; do not assign a full call number from a title alone.
researchCards.preparationGate: Obtain current cataloging expertise and a chosen lawful record sample before authoring an assessed lesson.

researchCards.question: Why is the letter S insufficient to identify a subject?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Compare the S and T examples from the two schemes. Write a reference containing scheme, institution or variant, edition, and code.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Keep each meaning attached to its own source; candidate atlas homes do not establish equivalence.
researchCards.preparationGate: Confirm the intended local audience and current vocabulary before importing any local scheme.

researchCards.question: How can one item have one shelf location and several subject routes?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Sketch a record with a classification field and several independently sourced subject headings; identify which values change physical location and which support topic discovery.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Keep controlled headings and classification distinct; do not invent an FNHL term.
researchCards.preparationGate: Choose an actual accessible catalog record and inspect its rights, current names and audience with qualified local input.

researchCards.question: What does a public project record establish about using a particular recording?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Read the public English project metadata and list the named authority, activity limits and outstanding asset-specific questions.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Distinguish discovery from permission, and a community-issued label from atlas review. Public metadata does not make an app asset public-domain material.
researchCards.preparationGate: No media selection, reproduction or adaptation until exact asset conditions and the relevant cultural authority/process are settled. No community contact is initiated.

researchCards.question: How do industrial production, hand making and household practice connect without being identical?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Outline research paths for a manufactured textile, a hand-made object and its household use. Name the different processes and the evidence each would need.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Use the class-level distinctions as discovery prompts, not practical instructions or claims that every process is taught.
researchCards.preparationGate: Select material, situated practice, competent reviewer and lawful assets before developing practical content.

researchCards.question: What changes when play is studied as rules, movement, learning or performance?
researchCards.proposedActivity: Compare invented descriptions of a game, a movement activity and a performance, then state the additional context needed before choosing a learning route.
researchCards.reviewCriterion: Do not collapse play into mathematical game theory or infer instruction from a shelf category.
researchCards.preparationGate: Choose a bounded activity and appropriately qualified review; actual movement/performance and learner observations remain unperformed.

implementationRequirements: Key external codes by scheme, variant and edition; never key by bare letters.
Keep classification placement distinct from multi-valued subject headings.
Store source wording/edition separately from atlas editorial labels and candidate relationships.
Keep source availability, cultural authority, reuse conditions, content review and publication decisions as separate fields.
Represent exact external project references without copying icons/templates or granting the atlas cultural authority.
Require fresh scoped review before changing the bound canonical registry or orientation inputs.
